related_questions.question: How long is the COVID vaccine effective?

text_blocks.snippet: The effectiveness of the COVID-19 vaccine in preventing infection varies. Original vaccines offered high levels of protection for a limited time, around six months, according to Pfizer's Phase 3 clinical trials. Updated vaccines, like the updated COVID-19 shots, are designed to target current variants and are considered up to date with a single dose for adults and older children with healthy immune systems. For younger children, multiple doses are needed to be considered up to date.

list.title: Original vaccines:
list.snippet: Studies showed the original Pfizer vaccine was about 91% effective in preventing COVID-19 for six months after the second dose.

list.title: Updated vaccines:
list.snippet: The most recent COVID-19 shots are not considered boosters, but rather updated vaccines targeting current variants, similar to how flu shots are updated annually. These updated vaccines aim to provide better protection against circulating strains.

list.title: Effectiveness against variants:
list.snippet: The updated vaccines offer better protection against the current variants circulating. For instance, the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine was estimated to be 33% effective against COVID-19-associated ED or UC visits among adults.

list.title: What's considered "up to date":
list.snippet: In the U.S., recommendations for what constitutes being "up to date" on COVID-19 vaccination vary based on age, previous vaccinations, and the vaccine manufacturer. Generally, adults and older children with healthy immune systems need one dose of the updated vaccine to be considered up to date. Younger children require multiple doses, with at least one being the updated vaccine.
